United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

description.narrative:
In December 2022, the UN General Assembly (UNGA) adopted a resolution to declare 2025 as the International Year of Glaciers’ Preservation (IYGP 2025). This was accompanied by the proclamation that March 21st of each year, starting in 2025, will be the World Day for Glaciers. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) were invited to facilitate the implementation of the International Year and the observance of the World Day. This initiative aims to raise awareness, pursue policy advocacy, and facilitate actionable and sustainable measures for the preservation of glaciers. Accordingly, a trust fund was established following the resolution, to be coordinated by the UN Secretary-General in partnership with UNESCO and WMO, to support countries in addressing issues related to the accelerated melting of glaciers and its consequences.
Following the establishment of a Trust Fund, UNESCO is actively supporting key activities in preparation for the implementation of the 2025 International Year of Glaciers’ Preservation. These elements play a crucial role in global outreach, communication, and coordination efforts, ensuring clear communication of the mission and activities for the year. The purpose of this project is to facilitate the implementation of activities for the International Year of Glaciers’ Preservation 2025. This initiative will specifically support various outreach activities, including the development of branding identity and design materials, such as logos and branding guidelines. Additionally, it will involve translating branding materials and the website into all UN languages.
Promotional materials, including tote bags, notebooks, pens, stickers, buttons, and water bottles, will be created to raise awareness. A video teaser for the IYGP will also be produced. The project will oversee the website’s domain name setup, development, graphic design, and ongoing maintenance. Lastly, an exhibition on glaciers and mountains will be organized to further engage and educate the public.
